From: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@synthara.ai>

Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 11:13:00 -04:00
Subject: Short request: evidence + workshop for ephemeral inference traces

Hi Naomi / Redwood team,

Quick context: Synthara is finalizing our SIG/CAIQ review and we have a compliance ask around ephemeral inference traces (debug snapshots and request-level metadata) that our auditors consider part of the data lifecycle. Our default ask is: evidence that Redwood deletes tenant-scoped debug traces on a tenant-defined TTL, with an auditable manifest and an automatic proof-of-delete process.

Concretely we need:
- A short playbook or runbook describing the delete pipeline (how snapshots are flagged, manifest generation, delete job, audit entry).
- A sample erase manifest (CSV or JSON) from a non-production tenant that shows what gets logged at deletion time (timestamps, object IDs, hashes).
- Confirmation whether retained debug traces can be scoped to a subset of inference events (selective sampling) vs. all requests.
- CAIQ / SIG pointers that map Redwood controls to the deletion workflow (if available).

Our timeline: auditor walkthrough week of Jul 28 — ideally we get artifacts & a 60‑minute workshop before then. Can you confirm whether this is possible and who we should coordinate with?

Thanks,
Sarah Lim
Head of Platform Security, Synthara
security@synthara.ai

(attachment: example_audit_ask.pdf)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. We can absolutely provide a deletion runbook and a sample erase manifest, and we can run a 60‑minute workshop before Jul 28.

Ask for scope clarification before we prepare artifacts: do you want tenant-wide retention behavior (all debug snapshots for tenant X) or targeted sampling only (e.g., 10% of requests / specific model eval jobs)? That affects what we pull for the sample manifest.

Plan I propose:
1) We prepare a 1–2 page runbook + sample erase manifest (non-prod) — deliver by Thu Jul 24 EOD PT.
2) Security/technical workshop (60 min) — schedule for Jul 25/26 or Jul 28 morning PT — agenda: runbook walkthrough, demo of manifest, Q&A on CAIQ/SIG mapping.
3) Provide CAIQ/SIG references mapping controls to the pipeline (inline doc) by workshop.

Looping in PrIyom (inference infra) and Kimberly (security PM) to help produce the artifacts and run the workshop. If that timeline works, please reply with the tenant name/ID and whether sampling is acceptable.

—Naomi

Hi Sarah / Naomi — I put together the technical artifacts we discussed and attached the runbook + an example erase manifest. High-level notes:

Attachment: deletion_runbook_v2.pdf (attached) — highlights:
- Trigger: snapshots are marked eligible for deletion when tenant TTL expires (tenant config in control plane).
- Manifest creation: a scheduled job compiles deletion_manifest.csv with columns: tenant_id, object_key, created_at, deleted_at, sha256_hash, deletion_job_id, operator_id (system user for automated jobs).
- Delete action: object storage lifecycle + an async erase job that removes KV traces and writes an audit event to the governance ledger (immutable append-only).
- Proof-of-delete: the job produces a signed manifest (HMAC) and the governance ledger stores a delete record with timestamp + manifest ref.
- Exceptions: customer-initiated legal hold overrides TTL (see manual hold section), and there is a documented safe-delete path for on-prem/private deployments where the customer operator runs the erase job under supervision.

Attachment: erase_manifest_sample.csv (attached) — sample rows (non-prod tenant):
tenant-789,trace-20250701-001,2025-07-01T03:01:22Z,2025-07-21T02:00:03Z,3a7f1c...,deljob-443,system

Compliance deliverables & timeline:
- Final runbook PDF + sample manifest by Thu Jul 24 EOD PT (attached).
- Workshop (60m): proposed Jul 25 10:00 AM PT or Jul 26 11:00 AM PT — please confirm.
- CAIQ/SIG mapping doc: short table mapping retention/deletion controls to CAIQ questions — will be shared during workshop.

Two quick technical clarifications for you that affect manifest contents:
1) If you need per-request request-body removal vs. request-metadata only, we need to know (request body removal has stronger SLOs and longer job time).
2) If sampling is used we include sampling rate and sample seed in manifest for reproducibility.

If you confirm tenant ID and sampling preference, we’ll finalize the sample manifest to match your scope.

Thanks,
PrIyom Das
Staff Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference
